title: Airport passenger traffic (Eurostat) and positions (OurAirports)
publisher: Eurostat (avia_paoa, from the national civil aviation authorities); OurAirports
license: Eurostat: free reuse (CC BY 4.0); OurAirports: public domain
description: Passengers carried by each airport of the map's countries that reports to Eurostat (scheduled and non-scheduled flights, arrivals plus departures, a year), placed by its ICAO code with the OurAirports database. Liechtenstein has no airport and Albania reports no figures.

title: CORINE Land Cover 2018, French overseas regions
publisher: SDES (French Ministry for the Ecological Transition), Copernicus; served by IGN (Géoplateforme)
description: 2018 land cover of Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana, Réunion and Mayotte, read from IGN's WMS (one image per inset). CORINE maps only French Guiana's coastal strip: the interior, Amazon rainforest, is classed as broadleaf forest.
used_for: Land cover of the French outermost regions

title: Climate of Europe 2000-2019: monthly temperature (ERA5) and precipitation (CHELSA), OpenGeoHub EcoDataCube
publisher: OpenGeoHub Foundation, from Copernicus ERA5 (ECMWF) and CHELSA (WSL)
license: CC BY 4.0 (data: Copernicus licence for ERA5, CC BY for CHELSA)
description: Monthly mean air temperature at 2 m (ERA5 reanalysis downscaled to 1 km with CHELSA) and monthly precipitation (CHELSA, 1 km), 2000 to 2019. Each month's file is read once: temperature sampled every 5 km, precipitation from its ~8 km overview; the decade means are kept (2000-2009 and 2010-2019; precipitation 2010-2018, the series stopping in mid-2019). Each hex takes the mean of the grid points inside it.
used_for: Temperature, warming, rainfall and rainfall change lenses

title: Land cover of Europe 2018, CORINE nomenclature (OpenGeoHub EcoDataCube)
publisher: OpenGeoHub Foundation (Geo-harmonizer project), from CORINE Land Cover (Copernicus) and LUCAS (Eurostat)
description: A 2018 land-cover map in the 44 classes of CORINE Land Cover, predicted at 30 m by machine learning on Landsat imagery, trained on CORINE and on the LUCAS survey points (Witjes et al., 2022). Its full-resolution tiles are read once and one 30 m pixel is kept every 480 m (the file's own overviews average class numbers, so they cannot be used for categories). Each hex's biome (forest, heath, grassland, cropland, wetland, town…) and its land shares come from a few hundred of those points inside it. The European Environment Agency's CORINE service could not be reached; this map uses the same nomenclature.
used_for: Shares of forest, cropland, pasture, built-up land
vintage: OpenGeoHub EU land cover 2018 (CORINE classes), 30 m map sampled every 480 m

title: ETOPO1 global relief model
publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (via ERDDAP)
description: Land elevation and sea depth, one point every two arc-minutes (~3.7 km; every arc-minute in the insets). Each hex's relief (flat, hills, mountains, peaks) comes from the mean and the spread (standard deviation) of the land points inside it.
vintage: ETOPO1, 1 arc-minute (every second point outside the insets)

title: Eurostat regional and city statistics
publisher: Eurostat (European Commission), from the national statistical institutes
license: Free reuse (Eurostat reuse policy, CC BY 4.0)
description: Population, age, GDP, value added and employment by branch of the NUTS 3 regions; unemployment, employment, degrees, household income, life expectancy and poverty of the NUTS 2 regions; population of the functional urban areas and core cities (Urban Audit). Read through Eurostat's dissemination API, since 2014. Tables: demo_pjan, demo_r_mlifexp, demo_r_pjanaggr3, demo_r_pjanind3, edat_lfse_04, ilc_peps11n, lfst_r_lfe2emprt, lfst_r_lfu3rt, nama_10_a10, nama_10_a10_e, nama_10_gdp, nama_10r_2hhinc, nama_10r_3empers, nama_10r_3gdp, nama_10r_3gva, urb_cpop1, urb_lpop1.
used_for: Population, GDP and jobs of cities, countries and regions

title: Places of 5,000+ inhabitants (GeoNames)
description: Populated places of 5,000+ inhabitants with their position and population. The cities of the countries without Urban Audit functional urban areas (Western Balkans, Cyprus, Iceland, Liechtenstein) come from here, and so do the searchable places of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Kosovo, which have no local administrative units in GISCO.
used_for: Cities of the Western Balkans, Cyprus, Iceland and Liechtenstein
Place search in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Kosovo

title: NUTS 2024 regions, countries, urban areas and local units (Eurostat GISCO)
license: Free reuse with attribution: © EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries
description: 1:3 million outlines of the NUTS 2024 regions (the countries and their NUTS 1, 2 and 3 regions), of the neighbouring countries (drawn in the haze), of the Urban Audit 2021 functional urban areas (a core city and its commuting zone), the core cities, and the local administrative units (LAU 2021: communes, Gemeinden, comuni…) with their 2021 census population.
used_for: Countries and regions on the map
vintage: GISCO: NUTS 2024, countries 2024, Urban Audit 2021, LAU 2021

title: Natural Earth 1:10m (lakes, rivers, neighbours of the outermost regions)
description: Lakes and rivers, with the European supplements, and the countries next to the outermost regions in their insets (Morocco, Suriname, Brazil). Files pinned to natural-earth-vector v5.1.2.

title: Natural Earth 1:10m roads and railroads
description: Motorways, major roads and main railways, as 1:10m lines. They are drawn as map decoration (roads and rails from hex centre to hex centre), not as statistics: the lines come from older Natural Earth releases and carry no traffic or operator. Files pinned to natural-earth-vector v5.1.2.
used_for: Motorways and major roads on the map

title: Seaport freight (Eurostat), placed with Wikidata and UN/LOCODE
publisher: Eurostat (maritime transport statistics, from the national authorities); Wikidata; UNECE UN/LOCODE
license: Eurostat: free reuse (CC BY 4.0); UN/LOCODE: free reuse (UNECE); Wikidata: CC0
description: Gross weight of goods handled by each port of the map's countries that reports to Eurostat (thousand tonnes a year, unloaded plus loaded), each country's latest complete year (the latest year in which at least 70% of the ports that reported the year before report too). Eurostat names a port by its UN/LOCODE; the port is placed at the Wikidata place carrying that code, or, where Wikidata has none, at the code's coordinates in the UN/LOCODE list (release 2024-2; it has a few misplaced entries, e.g. Delfzijl and Kaskinen, which is why Wikidata comes first). Rows that are not one place ("other ports", offshore installations, confidential totals) are left out.
used_for: Ports on the map, ranked by tonnage

title: Power plants of Europe (powerplantmatching, with the WRI Global Power Plant Database)
publisher: PyPSA powerplantmatching (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, TU Berlin and contributors); World Resources Institute
description: Every power plant and storage site of powerplantmatching v0.9.1, a merge of the JRC Open Power Plants Database (JRC-PPDB-OPEN), ENTSO-E, the Global Energy Monitor trackers, Open Power System Data, national registers (such as Germany's Marktstammdatenregister) and the WRI Global Power Plant Database: fuel, technology, capacity, position, commissioning and retirement years. Iceland and Cyprus, which it does not cover, come from the WRI Global Power Plant Database 1.3 (2021). Only plants in service in 2026 of at least 1 MW are read, and batteries only with a commissioning year from 2012 (the storage database behind them also lists undated projects).
used_for: Nuclear, hydro, coal, gas and geothermal plants
vintage: powerplantmatching v0.9.1; WRI Global Power Plant Database 1.3

title: Eurostat structural business statistics by NUTS 2 region
publisher: Eurostat (European Commission), from the national statistical institutes
license: Free reuse (Eurostat reuse policy, CC BY 4.0)
description: Persons employed in the local units of enterprises by NACE Rev. 2 section and division, for the NUTS 2 regions, 2021 onwards (table sbs_r_nuts2021). Business economy only: sections B to N and the market parts of P, Q, R and S. Not published for Switzerland, Liechtenstein and the Western Balkans except Serbia and North Macedonia; figures withheld as confidential are flagged.
used_for: City View districts: industry specialities (divisions) of each city's region
vintage: Eurostat SBS by NUTS 2 region (sbs_r_nuts2021), 2024; updated 2026-09-30

title: World Heritage List (UNESCO World Heritage Centre)
publisher: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, via the UNESCO open data portal
description: Every property on the World Heritage List: name, category (cultural, natural or mixed), year of inscription, States Parties, area, In Danger status and the position of each component of serial and transboundary properties. Only the properties with at least one State Party on the map are read.
vintage: World Heritage List after the 2026 session (1,273 properties)

title: Eurostat city statistics (Urban Audit)
publisher: Eurostat (European Commission), from the national statistical institutes
license: Free reuse (Eurostat reuse policy, CC BY 4.0)
description: Population by age group, median age, citizenship and country of birth, highest level of education (ages 25-64), journeys to work by mode of transport and labour market of the functional urban areas and their core cities, 2021 Urban Audit geography, read through Eurostat's dissemination API. Tables: urb_ceduc, urb_clma, urb_cpop1, urb_cpopcb, urb_cpopstr, urb_ctran, urb_leduc, urb_llma, urb_lpop1, urb_lpopcb, urb_lpopstr, urb_ltran.
used_for: City View citizens: generations, commute, education and origins
